title: Recursion: write and debug algorithms
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: termination — Reaching a condition where the algorithm stops.
recursive step — Processing part of a problem before calling the function on a simpler input.
precondition — An assumption or input rule required for an algorithm.
stack overflow — A failure that can occur when too many active calls consume stack space.
integer division — Division discarding any fractional part of the result.

blocks.title: Find the smallest problem
blocks.text: A positive single-digit number needs one digit. So n < 10 is our base case.

blocks.title: Make progress
blocks.text: For n ≥ 10, integer division by 10 makes the number shorter: 4827 → 482 → 48 → 4.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model CountDigits(582). Why is integer division essential?
Worked example · Calls
blocks.text: 582 → 58 → 5. Each integer division by 10 discards the last digit.
